# Oven management

**The bake is two halves and they are two different jobs.** Marlow splits it at
the moment the lid comes off, and insists that almost every complaint about a
bake belongs to one half or the other, never to both.

- **First half — 30 minutes, lidded, 250 °C.** The dough is still expanding, and
  the only job is keeping the crust soft enough to let it. They call a covered pot
  "steam you do not have to think about" and prefer it to a tray of water for
  anyone with fewer than fifty bakes behind them.
- **Second half — 25 minutes, uncovered, 230 °C.** Colour and crust, nothing else.
  Oven spring is finished by now; anything done here cannot rescue a loaf that did
  not rise.
- **Pulled at 98 °C internal.** They give this as a single number rather than a
  range, and say a thermometer settles more arguments in a bakery than any other
  tool.

The rule they use to attribute a fault: **pale, soft crust is the second half;
flat, dense loaf is the first half or earlier.** They will not accept "my oven
runs cold" until someone has measured it, and they treat a preheat under 45
minutes as the most common unmeasured error in home baking.

This assumes a dough at the hydrations in [crumb and hydration](crumb-and-hydration.md);
where a bake sits in a beginner's sequence is in
[teaching a first bake](teaching-a-first-bake.md).
